doc.title: Jackie Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

title: Milt Hinton and how recording has changed
summary: He praises Milt Hinton and comments on more technology and microphones in studios.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: And when you look at some of these great artists like Milt Hinton and so forth — it must be such a thrill to play—
Yes. Milt has to be in every home there is, and so justifiably so. He is just such a great artist and human being. He’s just wonderful.
Has recording, the process of it, changed significantly over the years, since you started recording? The actual studio presence?

Well I imagine it has come to a lot of technical changes. They use a lot more technologies now. I wasn’t there in the beginning like say Milton or a lot of the other musicians were, but I could tell that they utilize a lot more things, you know, machinery and microphoning and things like that — unless you tell them that you don’t want all that. You know sometimes you can tell them, if you’re being over miced or if there’s something wrong with the way they’re doing it, you could make suggestions. But they’re going to do what they’re going to anyway.
Yeah. They say, “Yeah, yeah,” and then after you leave it’s like—
